html:
The Nestucca were a band of the Tillamook people, who lived around Nestucca Bay and the Nestucca River on the north coast of Oregon. Like other Tillamook they spoke a Salish language, the southernmost of the Coast Salish tongues.

They lived in plank houses near the shore, fished for salmon, gathered shellfish and roots, and travelled by canoe. Their kin the Nehalem lived to the north. Disease brought by traders in the late 1700s and early 1800s killed most of them. In the 1850s the survivors were moved onto the Coast Reservation, and their descendants belong to the Siletz and Grand Ronde tribes.
